title: Simplifying surds
keyIdea: √(a × b) = √a × √b, so a square factor can come out of the root: √72 = √36 × √2 = 6√2. Take out the biggest square factor. Like surds add like like terms, and 1/√2 = √2/2 after multiplying top and bottom by √2.

kid: √12 means the side of a square with area 12. It is not a whole number.
Cut that square into 4 equal squares. Each has area 3, so each side is √3. Two of them make the big side, so √12 = 2√3.
Look for square numbers inside: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36. 50 = 25 × 2, and √25 = 5, so √50 = 5√2.
Surds with the same root add like apples: 2√3 + 5√3 = 7√3.
adult: Because √(ab) = √a × √b for a, b ≥ 0, write the number as a square times the rest and root the square: √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2. A surd is in simplest form when the number under the root has no square factor above 1.
Use the largest square factor, or keep going until none is left: √72 = √(9 × 8) = 3√8 = 3 × 2√2 = 6√2. The rule also runs backwards: √2 × √8 = √16 = 4, and 3√5 = √(9 × 5) = √45.
Only like surds combine when adding: √12 + √27 = 2√3 + 3√3 = 5√3. To rationalise a denominator, multiply top and bottom by the surd: 6/√3 = 6√3/3 = 2√3, and 1/√2 = √2/2.

Common mistakes: taking the square out without rooting it (√50 = 25√2); stopping at a factor that still holds a square (3√8); writing √a + √b = √(a + b); adding the numbers under like roots (5√6 for 5√3); and not dividing by the bottom when rationalising.

familyTip: Draw a square on squared paper with area 8 by tilting it (corners 2 across and 2 up). Then build a 2 × 2 grid of those tilted squares. Its area is 32 and its side is 2√8 = 4√2. Measure both sides with a ruler.

worked.title: Simplify √72, then √72 + √8 and 6/√2.
steps: Square factors of 72: 4, 9, 36. The biggest is 36, and 72 = 36 × 2.

pool.explain: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 has no square factor. 18 = 9 × 2 and 20 = 4 × 5 both do, so they simplify to 3√2 and 2√5.

pool.explain: 1/√3 × √3/√3 = √3/3 ≈ 0.58. 1/3 drops the root, and 3√3 is about 5.2.

pool.prompt: Why is 3√8 not the simplest form of √72?
choices: A surd can never have a number in front
pool.hint: Look at the number left under the root.
pool.explain: 8 = 4 × 2, so 3√8 = 3 × 2√2 = 6√2. Using the biggest square, 36, gets there in one step.
